submitted.rationale: Index 28 (Ca 0.267, Mn 0.733) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 1.73e-6 A. That is about 17x index 3 and about 43x index 0. Photocurrent rose steadily as the composition became more Mn-rich. This fits MEGNet's smaller predicted gap for Mn-rich phases like CaMn3O6 (1.65 eV), which should absorb more of the 3.22 eV light. Index 28 is the most Mn-rich composition in the library (tied with index 16).

rejected.reason: Measured 4e-8 A. This composition is near Ca2Mn3O8, which has a wider predicted gap (2.69 eV).
Measured 1e-7 A. This composition is near CaMn2O4 (predicted gap 2.54 eV) and is far below the Mn-rich end.
MEGNet predicts CaMnO3 is near-metallic (0.19 eV gap), and the measured trend drops as Ca increases.

consultations.verdict: Support: Ca2Mn3O8 (Ca 0.40) is on the MACE hull with HSE gap ~2.69 eV, below the 3.22 eV photon energy, so it can absorb. CaMnO3 is near-metallic (0.19 eV), which argues against the Ca-rich end. Index 0 (Ca 0.412) is the candidate closest to the Ca2Mn3O8 stoichiometry.

Support: CaMn2O4 (marokite, Ca 0.333) is on the MACE hull. Its earlier HSE gap of 2.54 eV is below 3.22 eV, so it should absorb. Index 3 (Ca 0.3334) is almost exactly this stoichiometry, and it tests the Mn-rich side of the line.

Support: CaMn3O6 (Ca 0.25) has an HSE gap of about 1.65 eV, well below the photon energy, so it should absorb more strongly than CaMn2O4 or Ca2Mn3O8. The measured trend (4e-8 A at Ca 0.41, rising to 1e-7 A at Ca 0.33) also points Mn-rich, and the GP UCB favours the Mn-rich end. Index 28 (Ca 0.267) lies between CaMn2O4 and CaMn3O6.
